content: OpenAI is facing a new wave of lawsuits from eight US states that accuse the company of harming children and misleading customers about the safety of ChatGPT, as reported earlier by Reuters. The lawsuits, filed separately by Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana, allege OpenAI unlawfully put profits over safety when developing ChatGPT. The string of complaints claims that OpenAI violated local consumer protection laws by failing to warn customers about the dangers of ChatGPT, citing several lawsuits filed by the family members of teens and adults that allege the AI chatbot played a role in their loved ones’ deaths. They allege that while OpenAI misleadingly presented ChatGPT as a “safe, youth-appropriate tool that puts safety first,” it was actually “dangerous to vulnerable users” — including by “degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships.” Additionally, the states accuse OpenAI of collecting data from minors and not doing enough to keep underage users from using the chatbot. The lawsuits also cite recent rogue AI hacking incidents as evidence of OpenAI’s alleged “recklessness.” “OpenAI has devolved from its original mission as a public-first nonprofit that prioritized safety into a cautionary tale about what can happen when the development of a tool as powerful as AI is driven not by safety, but by a profit‑at‑all‑costs mindset that sidelines essential safeguards,” Arizona’s lawsuit claims. In an emailed statement to The Verge, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says the company has “built industry-leading age-specific protections” into ChatGPT: > While no system can be perfect, we’ll continue to work with experts to inform our work and build additional safeguards, such as the parental controls, break reminders and age-appropriate model protections that exist today. We’re committed to working with states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry - not just one company. The states are asking the courts to force OpenAI to pay a series of civil penalties and to stop misleading the public about the safety of ChatGPT. Some states are also seeking the deletion of unlawfully collected personal data. Update, October 14th: Added a statement from OpenAI.
chineseTitle: 八个州起诉 OpenAI，称 ChatGPT 对儿童不安全

chineseContent: 据路透社早些时候报道，OpenAI 正面临来自美国八个州的新一波诉讼，指控该公司伤害儿童并在 ChatGPT 的安全性方面误导客户。这些诉讼分别由爱荷华州、堪萨斯州、内布拉斯加州、西弗吉尼亚州、阿肯色州、亚利桑那州、爱达荷州和蒙大拿州提起，指控 OpenAI 在开发 ChatGPT 时非法将利润置于安全之上。这一系列投诉称，OpenAI 未能警告客户有关 ChatGPT 的危险，违反了当地消费者保护法，并援引了青少年和成年人家庭成员提起的几起诉讼，指控 AI 聊天机器人在他们亲人的死亡中发挥了作用。他们声称，虽然 OpenAI 误导性地将 ChatGPT 描述为“安全、适合年轻人的工具，将安全放在第一位”，但它实际上“对弱势用户构成危险”​​，包括“降低批判性思维能力、鼓励偏执和妄想、提供危险的医疗建议以及促进不健康的行为和关系”。此外，各州还指责 OpenAI 收集未成年人的数据，并且没有采取足够措施阻止未成年用户使用聊天机器人。这些诉讼还引用了最近发生的流氓人工智能黑客事件作为 OpenAI 所谓“鲁莽”的证据。亚利桑那州的诉讼称：“OpenAI 最初的使命是作为一个公共第一的非营利组织，将安全放在首位，变成了一个警示故事，告诉我们当像人工智能这样强大的工具的开发不是由安全驱动，而是由忽视基本保障措施的不惜一切代价盈利的心态驱动时，会发生什么。” OpenAI 发言人 Drew Pusateri 在发给 The Verge 的电子邮件声明中表示，该公司已在 ChatGPT 中“构建了行业领先的针对特定年龄的保护措施”： > 虽然没有一个系统是完美的，但我们将继续与专家合作
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
